name: Djiwarli
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Austin, Peter K. A Grammar of Jiwarli (unpublished ms., SOAS) and Austin 1992, A Dictionary of Jiwarli, Western Australia (with grammar/phonology sketch) - neither retrievable online in this hunt.

new_statements.quote: All words in Jiwarli must end in a vowel, and all words begin with one and only one consonant. In general, stress (emphasis) falls on the first vowel of a word. So, for example, we have the word mandharda 'person' which is pronounced as man-dha-rda with stress on the first syllable man. Do not put emphasis on later syllables as this sounds very unnatural in Jiwarli (in English we might be tempted to pronounce this word as man-dha-rda, but if you pronounce it this way it would sound very strange to someone who speaks Jiwarli).
new_statements.citation: Austin, Peter K. 2015 (published 2015-06-17, modified 2022-04-11). 'Spelling'. Jiwarli: a blog about the Jiwarli language of Western Australia (jiwarli.com), by P. K. Austin. https://jiwarli.com/spelling/
new_statements.locator: page 'Spelling', final paragraph before the comments (text file lines 182-190)
new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress falls on the first syllable (first vowel) of the word; later syllables are not stressed.
new_statements.exceptions: Hedged with 'In general'; no specific exceptions given.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (pronunciation guide for the practical orthography); the example is a citation-form trisyllable. The source is a web pronunciation/spelling page by the primary field linguist (Austin worked with the last speaker Jack Butler 1978-1986), not the unpublished reference grammar.
new_statements.identity_note: Statement is about Jiwarli proper (djiw1241) as spoken by Jack Butler (Henry River, WA); Austin treats Jiwarli, Thiin, Warriyangka and Tharrkari as the Mantharta group and suggested Jiwarli and Thiin may be dialects of one language (Thieberger 1996: 106). The source is P. K. Austin's own web pronunciation guide (jiwarli.com/spelling/), not the unpublished reference grammar.
